audit_findings.title: Entrust earnings and financing may not be on the same run-rate basis
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.388 billion purchase price and $1.383 billion increase in debt; run-rate OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor projects partial-period Entrust earnings, interest, integration costs and maintenance investment as though they represent a recurring annual OE level.
audit_findings.evidence: On January 23, 2026, ("Signing Date"), Leidos, Inc. entered into a stock purchase agreement with KENE Holdings, L.P. and KENE Parent Inc. ("Entrust") to acquire all of the shares of Entrust for a purchase price of $ 2.4 billion in cash, subject to customary adjustments for Entrust’s cash, debt, transaction expenses and net working capital.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated: Entrust closed March 27, 2026, while the July balance sheet includes the acquisition and permanent financing but the earnings record includes only a partial post-close period. The direction depends on whether full-year Entrust owner earnings exceed the omitted full-year interest, integration and maintenance requirements. The transaction equals 15.2% of the $15.733 billion base equity value, and the bull value of $134.20 is only $1.15 per share above the market price, so a plausible run-rate correction can change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Construct full-year Entrust OE from acquired operating cash earnings less maintenance capital, include annual interest on the $600 million and $800 million notes, normalize integration and purchase-accounting effects, and rerun all scenarios from the resulting combined-company anchor.

audit_findings.title: A one-time OBBBA cash-tax benefit may remain in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $265 million filed reduction in fiscal-2025 income taxes payable versus the pre-OBBBA estimate and $91 million expected fiscal-2026 cash-tax reduction; catch-up portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring cash-tax reduction increases reported operating cash flow and OE; capitalizing it through the forecast overstates recurring OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: On July 4, 2025, the OBBBA implemented several corporate tax law changes, including but not limited to, (1) restoring the ability to immediately expense U.S. research and development costs; (2) allowing certain taxpayers an election to deduct the unamortized balance of U.S. research and development costs capitalized in prior years; and (3) reinstating one hundred percent bonus depreciation for eligible property.
audit_findings.explanation: A material tax benefit is demonstrated, including the election concerning previously capitalized R&D. What remains unresolved is how much of the $1,063.6 million anchor reflects the one-time catch-up rather than sustainable prospective deductions. The filed $91 million expected fiscal-2026 cash benefit alone equals 8.6% of anchor OE, readily enough to alter the scenario values and the narrow bull-case premium to market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile cash taxes embedded in the anchor to tax expense and balance-sheet tax movements, isolate the benefit from deducting prior-year capitalized R&D, retain only recurring prospective OBBBA effects, and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Unquantified antitrust exposure is absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: Any uninsured fine, settlement, disgorgement or defense cost would reduce the equity bridge, while procurement restrictions or reputational damage could reduce future OE or growth.
audit_findings.evidence: It is not possible at this time to determine whether we will incur, or to reasonably estimate the amount of, any fines, penalties, or further liabilities in connection with the investigation pursuant to which the subpoena was issued.
audit_findings.explanation: The DOJ criminal antitrust investigation and subpoena covering three government procurements are demonstrated, but the company states that liability cannot be determined or reasonably estimated. The record supplies no accrual, probable loss, insurance recovery or outcome range from which materiality can be established. It therefore remains an unresolved equity claim rather than a demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain subsequent DOJ status, quantified legal accruals and defense costs, applicable insurance or indemnification limits, and procurement consequences; then add a probability-weighted reserve or scenario adjustment if supportable.

audit_findings.title: Contract-estimate catch-ups may have been treated as recurring earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $84 million net favorable fiscal-2025 pretax EAC impact and $41 million fiscal-2025 prior-obligation revenue; fiscal-2026 first-half net favorable EAC impact was $17 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Favorable estimate revisions increase current earnings and OE without representing current-period production; projecting the affected anchor capitalizes them into forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal 2025, 2024 and 2023, revenue recognized from performance obligations satisfied in previous periods was $ 41 million, $ 13 million and $ 8 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Favorable catch-ups are demonstrated, although the record does not establish that every adjustment is nonrecurring or identify the exact amount embedded in the $1,063.6 million anchor. The $84 million fiscal-2025 net favorable pretax impact equals 7.9% of anchor OE, while the sharp fall to $17 million in the fiscal-2026 first half supports normalization review. That scale is capable of moving the bull value below the $133.05 market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace each anchor-period EAC write-up, write-down, variable-fee revision and prior-obligation item into OE; replace exceptional net benefits with a supportable multi-year normalized level and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Open DCAA audits could create cash refunds beyond recorded reserves
audit_findings.mechanism: Disallowed costs exceeding recorded reserves would produce refunds or reduced collections outside normalized OE and could also lower future contract margins.
audit_findings.evidence: Although we have recorded contract revenues based upon an estimate of costs that we believe will be approved upon final audit or review, we cannot predict the outcome of any ongoing or future audits or reviews and adjustments and, if future adjustments exceed estimates, our profitability may be adversely affected.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates that DCAA indirect-cost audits remain open for fiscal 2024 and later, while management states that reserves are adequate. No questioned-cost amount, reserve balance or historical settlement range is supplied. Consequently, the possibility is real but the record cannot establish either an additional liability or its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain unresolved questioned costs by audit year, the recorded audit reserve, unbilled rate variances and historical settlements; deduct any probable reserve shortfall from equity and adjust OE if disallowances change sustainable margins.

audit_findings.title: Deferred-compensation obligations may require a net balance-sheet deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: $530 million gross combined deferred-compensation and purchase-obligation payments, equal to $4.07 per diluted share and 3.4% of base equity value; net deferred-compensation shortfall unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Deferred compensation already charged to past earnings but payable later requires an equity-bridge deduction to the extent unfunded and not captured in forecast OE; ordinary executory purchase obligations remain operating costs and should not be deducted.
audit_findings.evidence: As of January 2, 2026, future payments on our deferred compensation arrangements and purchase obligations for long-term purchases and service agreements were $101 million, expected to be paid in fiscal 2026, and $429 million expected to be paid thereafter.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates $101 million due in fiscal 2026 and $429 million thereafter, but combines deferred compensation with purchase commitments. It also identifies rabbi trusts without disclosing the deferred-compensation liability and matching trust assets needed to calculate a net claim. The $530 million gross ceiling could affect the conclusion, including eliminating the bull-case premium, but the attributable unfunded amount cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Separate deferred-compensation liabilities from purchase commitments, identify corresponding cash, securities and share-unit assets in each rabbi trust, determine whether future OE includes settlement cash flows, and deduct only the net unfunded amount not otherwise captured.
